lesson.title: The profiling rule
lesson.summary: Apply the profiling override within Annex III without extending it to every AI system.

prerequisites.reason: The override depends on whether the system performs profiling as defined by the incorporated law.
The learner must know which paragraph 3 gateway is displaced by the profiling rule.

blocks: The **profiling override** says an AI system referred to in Annex III is always high-risk where it performs profiling of natural persons, notwithstanding paragraph 3's gateway.
Its scope matters: it is not a rule that every AI system anywhere becomes high-risk merely because it profiles. First establish the relevant Annex III use.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3), final subparagraph; Article 3(52)

blocks: Recall profiling: automated personal-data processing evaluating personal aspects, with context-specific cross-referenced definitions. The record must show what is evaluated rather than inferring profiling from every name in a file.

Northbridge's applicant reliability predictor performs a personal evaluation. A purely alphabetical list operation has different facts. Human final approval does not erase the earlier automated evaluation.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3), final subparagraph; Article 3(52)

blocks: Fictional case: the system is stipulated to fall within Annex III recruitment and predicts personal suitability. A claimed narrow-task or preparatory condition cannot overcome the profiling override.
Do not rearrange the test to accept a convenient condition before checking profiling. Record the exact personal evaluation and the corresponding listed use.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3), final subparagraph; Article 3(52)

blocks: Changed case: profiling is shown, but no Annex III purpose has been established. Investigate the listed-use route and any product route, along with other law. Do not use this override as a universal classification formula.
A result that the override does not apply is narrower than 'no obligations'. Other AI Act duties and personal-data rules can still matter.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3), final subparagraph; Article 3(52)

questions.prompt: What must be established before applying the paragraph 3 profiling override?

options.blocks: A relevant Annex III system and personal profiling
options.reason: The sentence is expressly scoped to Annex III systems.

options.blocks: Only that software handles a person's name
options.reason: A name alone proves neither profiling nor the listed purpose.
The Annex III comparison is essential.
